power.title: Power Analysis Check

table.text: SE/SD is the ratio of the mean cluster-robust standard error to the empirical standard deviation. Single-event power is Gray's test on each cause. Scenario Estimator Bias SE/SD Coverage Power ρ Power (single) Null, n=250 stacked 0.01 0.95 0.94 0.06 (type I) 0.06 / 0.04 Null, n=600 stacked -0.00 0.97 0.93 0.07 (type I) 0.07 / 0.06 Divergent, n=600 stacked 0.01 0.96 0.95 0.64 0.68 / 0.60 the same condition. Sample sizes were chosen per experiment: n = 250 for the null scenario to stress type I control at a moderate sample size, and n = 600 for the effect scenarios so that the single-event comparator tests have mid-range power, where comparisons are informative.

Table 1 confirms approximate unbiasedness (|bias| ≤ 0.01), calibrated standard errors (SE/SD 0.95-0.97), near-nominal coverage (0.93-0.95), type I error consistent with the nominal 0.05 up to Monte Carlo error (0.06-0.07; Monte Carlo SE ≈ 0.01 at 500 replicates), and power comparable to the single-event tests (0.64 versus 0.68/0.60), consistent with the bounded, negative-covariance efficiency trade-off of Section 3.4. The null-scenario rows at n = 250 and n = 600 are essentially identical, confirming that calibration is not sample-size dependent over this range.
